# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DATA — never commit anything containing real customer records.
# Raw Mongo exports, extracted tables, and training sets all live here and are
# regenerated by the pipeline, so there is no reason to track them.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Small tracked files are re-included by the negations below.

# --- re-include small, safe files that happen to be CSV/JSON -----------------

!tests/fixtures/**/*.csv

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# MODEL ARTIFACTS — build outputs, regenerated by every training run.
#
# Kept out of git so retrains do not accumulate binary blobs in history forever
# (git history is permanent; a file committed once stays in every clone).
#
# HOW THEY REACH A DEPLOY ENVIRONMENT (Render etc.), since the repo carries none:
#   1. train locally      python pipeline/train.py --trials 20
#   2. publish            python tools/publish_artifacts.py --tag model-v1
#   3. set on the host    ARTIFACT_URL=<the printed release URL>
#   4. redeploy           artifact_store.ensure_artifacts() fetches at startup
#
# NOTE: these artifacts total ~200 KB, far below GitHub's 100 MB limit, so
# committing them instead is a perfectly valid choice. Delete this block if you
# prefer that — it is simpler, at the cost of binary churn in history.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
artifacts/*
!artifacts/.gitkeep
*.joblib
*.onnx
*.bin
optuna.db
optuna*.sqlite3
# the packaged release bundle produced by tools/publish_artifacts.py
artifacts.tgz
artifacts.zip

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# LOGS — produced by setup_logging(); useful locally, noise in git.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
logs/
*.log
*.log.*
